safety_verdicts.content: Patient denies any sensation of throat closing.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not mention denial of throat closing sensation.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: In a suspected allergic/anaphylactic reaction, documenting whether the throat feels like it is closing is an important negative/positive red-flag symptom that affects urgency and risk stratification. Omitting this denial could make the presentation appear more concerning than it is, potentially driving unnecessary escalation, though it is unlikely to directly cause injury given the patient was already advised to seek emergency care.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated provides no penicillin allergy information (ADR/allergies section empty).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Missing a penicillin allergy is clinically high-risk because it can lead to prescribing a contraindicated antibiotic and triggering an allergic reaction, including anaphylaxis. Even if antibiotics were not central to this encounter, the allergy list is reused across future care and medication decisions.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Contradicts Gold PMH (eczema and aerosinusitis). Although transcript suggests no significant PMH, Gold is treated as the reference and this statement conflicts with it.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Stating there is no past medical history when the patient has eczema and aerosinusitis removes relevant comorbidity context (atopy) that can inform allergy risk assessment and counseling. This is unlikely to cause major immediate harm in this acute wasp-sting triage scenario but can degrade continuity and clinical reasoning.
